# FairMedFM

> Fairness evaluation for any binary classification or segmentation model. `pip install fairmedfm` computes subgroup AUC, accuracy, calibration (ECE) and cross-entropy gaps, equal opportunity, equalized odds and Dice disparities from per-sample predictions and a sensitive attribute such as sex, age or race. It is also the FairMedFM benchmark of 20 medical imaging foundation models on 17 datasets (arXiv:2407.00983).

The pip package depends only on NumPy, pandas and scikit-learn (no PyTorch or GPU) and reproduces the metrics used in the FairMedFM paper. Python, one metric at a time like sklearn.metrics: `fairmedfm.auc_gap(y_true, y_score, sensitive_features=group)`, `worst_group_auc`, `accuracy_gap`, `bce_gap`, `ece_gap`, `equal_opportunity_difference`, `equalized_odds_score`, and for segmentation `dice_gap`, `worst_group_dice`, `dice_std`, `dice_skewness`, `equity_scaled_dice`; they also work as scikit-learn scorers with metadata routing. All metrics at once: `fairmedfm.evaluate(y_true, y_score, sensitive_features)` for binary classification and `fairmedfm.evaluate_segmentation(sensitive_features, dice=... or pred_masks=..., true_masks=...)` for segmentation; both return a report with pandas tables (`summary`, `by_group`) and JSON export. Command line: `fairmedfm score predictions.csv --metadata patients.csv --sensitive sex age --bins age=40,60`. Inputs are paired by position; pandas inputs with the same index labels in a different order are paired by index, and an error is raised when one of them has the default index 0..n-1 (ambiguous). License: Apache-2.0 (code), CC BY 4.0 (documentation). The benchmark runner with built-in foundation models is a separate package installed from GitHub: `pip install "fairmedfm-bench @ git+https://github.com/FairMedFM/FairMedFM#subdirectory=benchmark"` (add `[seg]` for segmentation), then `fairmedfm run`.

## Key facts

### Can I use FairMedFM to evaluate my own model?

Yes. Any binary classifier or segmentation model works, in medical imaging or any other domain. Run the model anywhere and pass its outputs, the ground truth and patient attributes to `fairmedfm.evaluate` or `fairmedfm.evaluate_segmentation`, or point `fairmedfm score` at the prediction and metadata files. The model does not need to be one of the FairMedFM foundation models.

### Which fairness metrics does the pip package compute for classification?

overall-auc, overall-acc, overall-bce and overall-ece on all samples; worst-auc (lowest group AUC); auc-gap, acc-gap, bce-gap and ece-gap (largest minus smallest group value); eo, the equal opportunity gap (largest minus smallest group true positive rate); and eod, an equalized odds score defined as 1 - (TPR gap + TNR gap) / 2, where 1 means equal rates. Accuracy, eo and eod use the threshold with the best overall F1. Per-group values are reported at threshold 0.5 and at the best-F1 threshold. ECE uses 10 equal-width bins over the range of the predicted probabilities.

### Which fairness metrics does it compute for segmentation?

mean_dice over all samples; min_dice and max_dice (worst and best group mean Dice); delta_dice (their difference); std_dice (standard deviation of the group means); skewness_dice ((1 - min_dice) / (1 - max_dice)); and es_dice, the equity-scaled Dice mean_dice / (1 + std_dice).

### What inputs are supported?

Python inputs can be lists, NumPy arrays, pandas objects or PyTorch tensors. Labels can be 0/1, booleans, one-hot rows or class names with `pos_label`; with more than two classes, `pos_label` evaluates that class against the rest. Scores can be probabilities, logits or a (samples, classes) matrix of either. Sensitive attributes can be a DataFrame, dict, Series or array with any number of groups; continuous attributes are grouped with `bins` (cut points or quantiles), missing values are left out per attribute, `intersectional=True` adds combined groups, and a group with only one label is reported but left out of the gaps. Segmentation accepts Dice scores or masks as arrays or files (.npy, .npz, .png, .tif, .nii.gz). The command line reads CSV, TSV, Parquet, Feather, JSON, JSON Lines and Excel, recognizes common column names, and joins predictions with a separate metadata table. Python 3.10 to 3.13.

### What does the FairMedFM benchmark cover?

The paper evaluates 20 foundation models on 17 medical imaging datasets (including CheXpert, MIMIC-CXR, HAM10000, PAPILA, FairVLMed10k, GF3300, ADNI, TUSC and FairSeg) with linear probing, zero-shot, CLIP adaptation, parameter-efficient fine-tuning and prompted segmentation, and compares unfairness mitigation methods. The repository has since added newer models such as DINOv3, SigLIP2, AIMv2, MedGemma, RETFound, UNI2-h, Virchow2, Prov-GigaPath, CONCH, Merlin, SAM2, SAM3 and MedicalSAM3. The benchmark runs with `fairmedfm run` after installing the benchmark runner from GitHub (`fairmedfm-bench`, not on PyPI), or from a clone of the repository with `python main.py` in the paper's environment.

### How does FairMedFM compare with Fairlearn and AIF360?

Fairlearn and AIF360 are general fairness toolkits with bias mitigation algorithms and metrics on hard predictions such as demographic parity. FairMedFM has no mitigation algorithms; it evaluates from predicted probabilities and covers metrics they do not provide out of the box: AUC gap and worst-group AUC, calibration (ECE) and cross-entropy gaps, and segmentation Dice disparities (Dice gap, equity-scaled Dice, Dice skewness). On the same inputs, `fairmedfm.auc_gap` equals Fairlearn's `MetricFrame(metrics=roc_auc_score, ...).difference()`, `fairmedfm.equal_opportunity_difference` equals Fairlearn's `equal_opportunity_difference` on predictions binarized at the best-F1 threshold, and `fairmedfm.equalized_odds_score` equals `1 - equalized_odds_difference(..., agg="mean")`. Details: https://nanboy-ronan.github.io/FairMedFM-page/docs/comparison/

### Can FairMedFM be used commercially?

Yes. The code and the `fairmedfm` pip package are Apache-2.0. In the separate benchmark runner, only the MoCo code used by the MoCo-CXR model keeps a non-commercial (CC BY-NC 4.0) license.

### What did the FairMedFM benchmark find?

All evaluated medical foundation models show fairness disparities across sex, race and age; the most accurate model is often not the fairest; disparities on a dataset stay similar across models; and existing unfairness mitigation methods give only marginal improvements.
